summary: Karma Lek Shé Drayang studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She served as an Assistant Professor at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and Numata Professor at Hawaiʻi in 2023.

Karma Phuntsho, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, Michael Aris, and David Seyfort Ruegg. He held research and fellow positions at the University of Cambridge from 2003 to 2008.

Karma Sonam Palmo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who served as abbot at the Young Lamas Home School around 1962 and at Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery, and founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling and Tekchen Lekshay Ling.

Karma Ura is a historian and Tibetologist who studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, Oxford, and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from 1999 to 2008.

Karsé Kongtrul studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Khakyab Dorje, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, whom he also taught alongside Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karuna Kusalasaya was an Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
Karunapati Tripathi was an Indologist who served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and President of the Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan.

Karunesh Shukla is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under V. P. Upadhyaya. He served as Reader and later Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University.

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz is a scholar of Tibetology, Central Asian studies, and religious studies who completed her PhD and Habilitation at the University of Bonn. In 1999 she became a professor at the University of Bern, later serving as Dean (2007–2010).

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Allahabad and the University of Oxford. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta in 1917 and as president of the Numismatic Society of India.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was an archaeologist and Indologist associated with the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute. He served as Officiating Government Epigraphist for India around 1931–1932 and as Deputy Director-General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1944).

Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indologist who studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. He served as a fellow at Elphinstone College, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1892–1893), and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College from around 1914 to 1945 and as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from around 1945 to 1976.

Kate Crosby is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at St Peter's College, Oxford, Cardiff University, the Buddhist Institute, SOAS University of London, and King's College London.
Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from SOAS University of London in 2008 and held a post at Birkbeck, University of London, attested in 2010.
Katharina Sabernig is a Tibetologist who earned her PhD at the University of Vienna in 2017 and held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul is a scholar of Tibetology, archaeology, and Indology who completed doctoral studies under Gudrun Bühnemann, also studying with Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.
